utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-04-84-PT, the Prosecutor versus Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good evening, Your Honour, for the Prosecution, David Re, accompanied by Gramsci Di Fazio, Gilles Dutertre, Katrina Gustafson, and our case manager Kim Fischer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Brahimaj, I appear, Ben Emmerson, together with Mr. Rod Dixon, Ms. Susan Park, and Ms. Marina Akenova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. And for the Defence of Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good evening, Your Honour, Gregor Guy-Smith appearing for Mr. Balaj with the assistance of Colleen Rohan and Natalie Van Den Berge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Richard Harvey appearing for Mr. Brahimaj, assisted by Ms. Antoniette Trapani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. I note that Mr. Haradinaj is on provisional release and two other accused are with us today. I would like to make sure that Mr. Balaj and Mr. Brahimaj are following this procedure in the language they understand. Mr. Balaj. THE ACCUSED BALAJ: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I do, and thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your response again because the -- your microphone was not activated. THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brahimaj. Well, this is the second Status Conference I have in this case since I was assigned to this case last -- July last year. Probably as all the parties will be aware, the case has -- as the start of the trial draws near, this probably will be the last Status Conference I have or the -- held on the part of the pre-trial Chamber. And it seems to be very likely that this case will be re-assigned to the Trial Chamber that will hear the case some time -- as soon as some time next week. And so my purpose today is to tidy up the -- all the outstanding motions and explore what can be done on the part of the Trial Chamber and make a clear list of the Trial Chamber of the outstanding matters. So, before I begin with the pending motions, first of all, I would like to inform the parties of the fact that the Trial Chamber just issued the decision on the Prosecution motion seeking leave to amend the indictment and -- which was filed November -- sometime November. So I hope the parties were handed over the courtesy copies of the decision. Can I get that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution has a copy, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So in that decision where the Chamber granted the Prosecution motion seeking leave to amend the indictment by substituting a second revised amended indictment filed on 10th November. And at the same time, the Chamber ordered the Prosecution to file its pre-trial brief by 26th of this month, which is two weeks' time from now, and ordered the Defence to file their respective pre-trial brief in two weeks' time from the date of the filing of the Prosecution's filing of their pre-trial brief. And that said, I would like to turn to other outstanding motions and deal with other items, and we'll hear from the parties if there's anything they would like to raise. First, there's a minor outstanding motion from the Prosecution seeking further directions pursuant to Trial Chamber's order regarding exhumations, which was filed just after I issued the order requesting assistance of UNMIK with certain investigation on 19th of October, 2006. Since I find -- found that the -- it would be a matter of course for the Defence to comply with the Rules and the practice of the Tribunal, I didn't act upon the order. But since -- at any rate, as the Defence teams have already carried out the exhumations in question, I think this motion is now moot; and -- unless there's a serious opposition from the Prosecution, I will dismiss the motion as moot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's entirely moot now, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's so decided. I'd like to turn to the Prosecution's motion for variation of the Trial Chamber order in relation to very -- in relation to confidential materials, which is related to witnesses K5 and K6. So if Mr. Re can wrap-up this situation in relation to that matter in brief terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It remains as we reported to Ms. Murnane in the Rule 65 ter conference yesterday. One of the witnesses is undergoing intense psychiatric care, and the other one has not been located through VWS. We will probably have a report from VWS, which we can furnish to the Defence and Trial Chamber next week. I can't take it any further today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When next week? A week's time from now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please. VWS has told us that they will have a report for us next week some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without prejudice to the merit of the case, without touching upon the merit of the case, I think the Prosecution can, as an interim measure, disclose immediately of the material in redacted form. Has it been done or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think we've prepared -- I think we have it prepared in redacted form. My -- I'm relying on my memory from about six weeks ago. I think it was ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But if you could immediately disclose those materials in redacted form and file a report in a week's time as to the feasibility of the interviews of those witnesses, and then the Trial Chamber can deal with it -- can act upon the written submission from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Most certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the Defence would have any say on -- in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that -- Your Honour, we've indicated that we've no objection to the service for the time being on an interim basis of the material in an redacted form, and it would be very useful to have it as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to emphasise this as an interim measure without prejudice to the merit or Balaj Defence's opposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So in a sense at the end of the day, the motion will inevitably remain pending until that process has been taken forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I take that the other -- the position of the other Defence to be the same? Thank you. Then the witness 30, a source, an agent, I take it that the interview took place with the source and the second person, and the interview with the witness 30 is still outstanding with the motion from the Prosecution with the extension of time. Can I hear the -- for the development from the Defence first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position is that witness -- witness interviews proceeded yesterday afternoon and this morning in respect of the second person and the source. I think Your Honour knows that the position of the Prosecution, as outlined at yesterday's Rule 65 ter meeting, is that further inquiries have recently been made and since the last filing of the Prosecution have been made again of witness SST730 and that he remains unwilling to make himself available for an interview by the Defence. And as the matter was left yesterday, we have requested that the Prosecution should nonetheless take from him a statement dealing with the bribe allegations so that we have in writing his account in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Until that time, the Defence motion for the -- for seeking the identity of the source and et cetera will remain?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Defence motion remains outstanding until, as we would submit, each of those matters has been finally concluded. But as Your Honour knows, the interview process in respect of those two individuals has taken place. The situation, as I think Your Honour is aware, is that when the last order was made in respect of those matters, the Trial Chamber was not aware of the involvement of the second person, but certainly we would -- we would request that this matter be left in abeyance until the Prosecution has completed that aspect of its inquiries that involves seeking a statement from SST730.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder if the Prosecution has responded to the Defence request, at least to have a written statement of witness 30. What's the position of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We've gone about as far as I think we can with this. Since we filed the application for an extension on the 5th of January, we have contacted the witness again. The witness made clear that he declined to speak to the Defence. There's nothing we can do that make him change his mind. We've spoken to him several occasions, asking him to speak to the Defence. Mr. Thomas Obruca, an investigator, we appended an application of Mr. Obruca to an application of the 5th of January. That information contains the gist of what he would say, that is basically denying that he ever provided that information to the second person or the source. But I'm afraid, Your Honour, it's not going to get any better, that's as far as we can take it, that the witness told Mr. Obruca that he denied it. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So then does it mean the Prosecution application for an extension of time to comply with the Trial Chamber's order is now -- is moot?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That, too, is moot. Yesterday, Ms. Murnane invited us to file something. If Your Honour wishes us to file something, we can file something in writing or we can advice you now. But it is essentially moot. We've taken it as far as we possibly could. We've made all good faith efforts to, A, get the witness to speak to the Defence; if that failed, B, take a statement from him. We can't get anything else at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the situation of the case that the case will be re-assigned to the Trial Chamber, I will like you to file a report in brief terms so that the Trial Chamber can act upon and the Defence can also act upon the written submission from the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, if I might. If I understand the exact position in which we are in presently, not only did Mr. Obruca speak with the witness, but he forwarded the witness a statement to be signed, which the witness refused to sign. And so we are left with a situation whereby the information contained in the interview between Mr. Obruca and the witness has yet to be memorialised in any fashion that I know of. If the report that Your Honour is requesting the Prosecution to file at this time includes a declaration from Mr. Obruca, I think that might bring the matter so some form of finality at this point with regard to as far as the things have gone. But I think we need to, for purposes of establishing a pure historical record of what's occurred here, have some -- have some indication of what was said as between Mr. Obruca and the witness in the form of a declaration signed by Mr. Obruca at this point. Since the witness himself apparently from the last declaration we received from Mr. Obruca has refused to sign such statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any observation from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with doing that. It would be similar to investigator's notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that would be helpful. Minutes ago I erroneously stated that the Defence motion is still outstanding. I just forgot that it has been denied. So the Defence can act upon, depending on what the Prosecution will say, in its report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the motion that remains technically outstanding is the Prosecution's motion for an extension of time within which it can comply with the order of the Trial Chamber made in response to the position of the Defence on the redaction motion. And Your Honour's quite right to say the redaction motion itself is to be disposed of with those conditions. The -- in effect, the outstanding issue or the framework within which the outstanding report is to be made is that there remains before the Trial Chamber a Prosecution application, but it is an application for an extension of time, to conduct interviews that now appear, as Mr. Re points out, to be clearly, interviews that won't take place and therefore that part of it is moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. To clarify the matter, in order to formally address the Prosecution motion for extension of time, I will grant the motion and I will give a week from now to -- I will order -- hereby order the Prosecutor to file its report in a week's time, by 19th of January, next Friday, and that's the alleged bribe attempt case. And then I'll turn to the issue of notes of witness 29. And what I was informed that the Prosecution had got a note from the witness and handed it over to the Defence; but apparently, according to the Defence, it does not seem to be the very note referred to in his statement. And the Prosecution is not sure whether it is the very note or not. That's the case so far I understood. I would like to know whether there is further development.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could Your Honour excuse me for just one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The situation is, Your Honour, as outlined. The witness provided us with some notes. It's four years since the statement was taken. We have contacted him in the last few days after receiving inquiries from Defence counsel. We double-checked with him. He is not entirely sure. He thinks he might have some other notes. We've asked him to go back and look in all places where notes might be and to please produce those to us. The notes -- any other notes may be in another location to where he is at the moment. It's not something which will occur straight away, but we've put the request in to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So -- I wonder the Prosecution is in a position to file any report in relation to that matter in a week's time or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A week would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At the same time, in relation to this matter, I'd like to ask the Defence whether in -- as to the practical use of this subpoena, if ordered. If the -- if the witness or the Prosecution would not be able to locate the notes, so what point would there be to -- for a subpoena to be issued?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the time that the application was made, the indications were that the witness was unwilling to produce notes that he had in his possession. Notes have now been produced, but has Your Honour knows there appears to be a divergence between the notes produced and the notes which the witness refers to in his witness statement. Now, the position as matters currently stand, as we would submit it, would certainly be premature at this stage for this motion to be either withdrawn or denied because further inquiries need now to be made. But I quite concede if a position should be arrived at that there are no other notes in existence and that is confirmed and clarified, then an order to produce that which does not exist would be a futile order. But at the moment, we don't have that position of clarity, because further inquiries are being made and the witness has indicated a willingness to ascertain whether the notes are in existence that can be voluntarily produce. It may be in due course that a coercive order is necessary, and given the indication that Your Honour that a week, or thereabout, should be an appropriate time-frame for a Prosecution report. We would again, in respect to this motion, simply invite you leave it pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The same treatment without pledging up on the merit of the case and wait for the Prosecution's report in relation to this matter. So I will expect the Prosecution to file its report by 19th of January, a week's time from now. I think I dealt with all the outstanding motions for now, and I will now turn to the disclosure issues. I was just informed by the Prosecution, just before I came into the courtroom, that Rule 66 disclosure has been all resolved. Can I hear from Mr. Re about it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The letter we furnished to the Senior Legal Officer earlier today said any remaining Rule 66 materials will be disclosed today. Today isn't quite over. We have a -- we are finishing burning them on to the CD-ROM and I think we have 322 documents, which will be put in Defence counsels' locker after this Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What can I say. Let's expect all the disclosure will be done by Prosecution by the end of today; and if there should be any disagreement, then who should report to the Trial Chamber as to the disagreement, if any? Prosecution -- it would be for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think Your Honour has the memorandum prepared on behalf of the Haradinaj Defence dated the 8th of January in preparation for the Rule 65 ter meeting and Status Conference. And at paragraphs 4 and 5 of that memorandum are set out under the headings Forensic Disclosure and Other Disclosure, a series of bullet points enumerating those aspects of the Defence 66(B) disclosure request that remain outstanding. And, certainly, we'll obviously need an opportunity to assimilate the material which the Prosecution proposes to disclose today; but having done that and as soon as we've done that, we will then report back to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- Trial Chamber, as to whether the items listed in our memorandum have all been complied with and insofar as there may be any difference between the parties, identifying that difference and making proposals as to how we might move forward to resolve it. We do say seven days, so by next Friday, for the Defence to make a short report to the Trial Chamber on the extent of Prosecution compliance with the requests listed in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the 8th of January memorandum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That would be very helpful, but my information is that the sixth bullet point on page 4, i.e., the names of the persons appearing in various photos, it's impossible for the Prosecution to provide with names.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think Your Honour will be aware that was the subject of some discussion yesterday at the Rule 65 ter meeting; and as I recall it, the way that the matter has been left is that the Prosecution would use its best endeavours to check a final time whether that truly is the position. Because the effect or the burden of the Prosecution's position is that photo line-ups were prepared from randomly selected photographs provided or obtained from the database of the Kosovo Protection Corps without the relevant investigator making or taking any steps to record the identities of the placebo photographs. That is, obviously, on its face a slightly surprising state of affairs, so a request has been made simply for the Prosecution to clarify whether indeed that is the position; and if it is, then plainly that is a request that is impossible to meet for whatever reason that is the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Re, does the material you are going to disclose by the end of today include the confidential materials in the Milosevic case which the Defence seeks to have access?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's a different matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a different --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- that the registry is disclosing that. We had communications today from the registry in relation to disclosure of that material. They would be in a better position to advise because we sent them the material on I think the 4th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I know that. Then I have to hear from the Defence in relation to that matter, as to the development.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before we turn to that matter, I should point out with regard to issues concerning photo line-ups, I delivered a letter to the Prosecution I believe about a day or two ago, requesting that the Defence receive all protocols that the Prosecution has with regard to the general identification procedures utilised by the OTP and other investigative agencies. And the reason I'm mentioning that at this point is because it seems to segue into some of the concerns that were raised by Mr. Emmerson with regard to the identification of the individuals, as he calls them, placebos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I didn't follow the protocols. What do you mean by protocols?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are -- from my understanding, within the OTP, a series of protocols and procedures that have been outlined for purposes of engaging in line-ups when they are at the investigative stage. We have asked for those protocols so that we can make a determination, because it probably will become an issue in this case as to whether or not the identification procedures that were used were appropriately done. And in order to make a determination of whether that's the case, we need to know what training experience and protocols the investigators were given prior to engaging in the photo line-ups procedures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I ask again the photo line-up proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. Generally speaking, the manner in which eye-witness identifications occur, apart from, let's say, that which occurs in the highly suspect situation of in court and in-dock identification, is that an individual be shown a photo-board. When shown a photo-board, the photo-board will have a number of photographs on it. There are a series of procedures that attend showing any witness that photo-board. For example, if the interviewer says: Will you please pick out the person who is guilty on the photo-board, that would be an inappropriate procedure, for example. As I understand it, having gone through this matter in a prior proceeding at the Tribunal, there are definite procedures that are either applied or not applied by the investigators who are engaged in showing people these photo-boards. So when I'm asking for photo line-up procedures, I'm asking for the information that has either been compiled by the Office of the Prosecutor or by other investigative agencies, as it relates to the manner in which the investigator is going to show any particular potential witness photo-boards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I hear from you, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. As Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith outlined, he sent us a letter and I'm dealing with it and I'll respond to it quite shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think there should be a deadline for that. You can respond very soon, at least in a week's time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I like to have some deadline instead of having those matters hanging around. Thank you. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, shall I now reply to Your Honour's question in relation to the confidential material arising out of the Milosevic case? I think that was the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- item you wanted me to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour will recall that on the 27th of September, a direction was given that all confidential interparties material relevant from the Milosevic case relating, that is, to the Kosovo part of the indictment be made available, subject to any Rule 70 objections that the Prosecution needed to bring to the attention of the registry. The position is that shortly before Christmas, a series of transcripts were sent out by the registry; but on examination, these transcripts are simply material which is already available on the judicial database; that is to say, redacted, open transcripts of witness testimony in the open part of the trial itself. During the course of yesterday's Rule 65 ter conference, the Prosecution indicated that it had complied with its duty to notify the registry by letter of Rule 70 objections in respect of that body of material and it appended a CD-ROM, but the registry apparently had not received it. And, therefore, the matter was left yesterday on the basis that as between the registry and the Prosecution, inquiries would be made. And I think Your Honour was provided with a copy of the letter that the Prosecution had, in fact, sent or drafted for the purposes of being sent to the registry. So in a sense, the resolution of this problem is a matter as between the registry and the Prosecution, because unless or until the Rule 70 communication has been received and acted upon, the registry are not in a position to make the disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I anticipate no problem on the part of the registry to disclose those confidential material, excluding the Rule 70 material, until Prosecution get the permission from the provider. And I haven't heard from the registry in relation to that matter, but I think as a matter of one or two days, speaking for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very grateful. Obviously, the sooner the material is available --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I have to check that matter with the registry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, the registry has been in contact with the Prosecution and, indeed, we have received the letter provided by Mr. Re during the 65 ter conference, in fact we received it earlier. But we are working on that and we hope that we'll be able to send the confidential material to the Defence sometime next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a very positive statement. Thank you. And then the remaining thing will be the -- will be for the Prosecution to get the permission or clearance from the provider. And I haven't read in detail about the -- the quantity of Rule 70 material, so can I ask how long would the Prosecution need to -- to take care of those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just can't say. We're seeking clearance. Your Honour, of course, was in the Milosevic case and is aware of the various institutions and governments and the length of time it sometimes takes them to reply to our request. We have -- we are saying that it's required in an upcoming trial. I -- unfortunately, I just can't give you an answer. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So in this matter -- in relation to this matter, instead of placing a specific deadline, I will recommend the Prosecution to deal with the matter as expeditious as possible. Any observation from the other Defence on this matter? No. Then -- and it is my understanding that the Prosecution will file today the motion for -- in -- 94 bis, i.e., the expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was filed, I'm told, at 3.55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has been filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But I advise the Trial Chamber and the colleagues from the Defence that there are four outstanding expert reports that we are in the business of obtaining at the moment, and we will be in a position to file those within two weeks. We have filed, I think, the eight that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. In the previous order, I ordered -- I'm not sure whether it was I or the Trial Chamber that -- it was ordered to the Prosecution to file the 92 bis/92 ter motion by today, but it is my -- I was informed that Prosecution would not do that. And I -- my query would be whether Prosecution would be able to file that motion by the time when it is -- it is filing the pre-trial brief, which means two weeks' time from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The motion, if I recall, said, if any, the qualification was "if any." We probably wouldn't be in a position to do it in two weeks. The reason for this is that there -- the Prosecution and Defence are in active discussion about the agreed facts and the scope and ambit of the trial. And once we have our witness list to the Defence with a pre-trial brief, they'll be in a much better position to assess where they go with agreements; and from that, we can sit down with the Defence and work out of court without filing a motion -- before filing a motion and possibly with the agreement of the Defence to which there would not be disagreement in relation to Rule 92 bis and ter. So if I could ask for some - what's the word? - laxity -- flexibility in dealing with this, because we are in discussions with the Defence. And it may assist in focusing on some of the issues in the trial rather than us filing something in a vacuum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The same will apply to the agreed facts and the adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence, as reported at the conference yesterday, are still obtaining instructions from their clients in relation to some of the agreed facts. We gave them, I think it was, 888 proposals for agreement, plus adjudicated facts from the Limaj judgement. The two -- the various parties are attempting to get them into something which we can file, which of course impacts on which witness we would call and impacts on the 92 bis and ter motions. So it basically comes as a package, the three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to that, I would like to -- appreciate the very constructive and fruitful discussion among the parties in relation to the agreed facts and adjudicated facts. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour I hope will have seen - and certainly if you haven't seen it yet, it is available - the letter which the Defence served on the Prosecution on the 9th of January, in compliance with the 13th of December order in respect to agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which also, as Your Honour will have seen, records specific proposals for reducing the scope of the indictment and shortening the trial. As far as the agreed facts proposals are concerned, some of them I think Your Honour is aware were served by the Prosecution very recently indeed. We expect to be in a position to keep that process continuing and to deal with each of the areas of the admissions the Prosecution has so far served and as well, as Your Honour will have seen, a certain and more general agreement of facts arising out of the Limaj judgement and otherwise concerning the military background issues in the case, all of which we anticipate have the potential to shorten the requirement for oral evidence in that regard. Your Honour, whilst I'm on my feet, may I mention one further matter allied to the Milosevic confidential material which we passed over without comment; and that is that in addition to the closed material in Milosevic, there is an ongoing disclosure process for the closed material in the Limaj case. And just if I may to put on record the position that the registry have indicated that that material will be served on the Defence within the coming days, in other words in what is the proposed timetable with respect to the confidential material in Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I would expect those materials to be disclosed as soon as possible. So the -- I would very much recommend the -- encourage the parties to go on the -- discussing the narrowing the scope of the case or the -- to reach on the agreed facts and adjudicated facts. So after the Defence would have filed their pre-trial brief on their part, the Prosecution would be in a better position to report to the Chamber as to the final agreement or the 92 bis -- its position in relation to 92 bis motion or something like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is one technical matter arising from Your Honour's discussion here, and that is the motion that directed us to file an adjudicated facts motion, if any, by today. I think the parties are in agreement if we were to ask jointly for Your Honour to suspend that portion of the order, to allow us to continue the discussions and to put something before the Trial Chamber at a later point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So I will now make an a ruling as to the deadline of the agreed facts or adjudicate facts; but in relation to the 92 bis or 92 ter motion, I would like to ask the Prosecutor to file its motion in a week's time from the filing of the Defence pre-trial brief. I think that's sufficient at least. Thank you. And due to the amendment of the indictment, not only by the recent one but also by the previous one, a further appearance to enter pleas to new charges by the accused will be necessary. But I think that can be done either at the time of the pre-trial conference or at any date the Trial Chamber would set. There would be no difficulty in that. I wonder if there's any issue in relation to the disclosure thing. Not anymore?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is Your Honour referring to the letter from the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, disclosure in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Other than the issues that we've already covered and also covered in the written memorandum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think there were no other issues that need a direction from Your Honour at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I dealt with all the agenda I noted down on my agenda. I'd like to hear whether -- from the parties if there's anything to raise now. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And how about the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Nor I at this stage. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I received a letter from Defence of Haradinaj and Brahimaj in relation to the Rule 67 or the alibi or the -- I haven't heard anything from Mr. Balaj's Defence. Do you have in mind to file anything in relation to that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the present time as I read the rule and the law, no. We are denying the charges against Mr. Balaj and expect the Prosecution to come to the table and attempt to meet its burden in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, then, as I said, this is my last Status Conference, and I wish everybody a very happy new year and good luck. The hearing is now adjourned.
